rulings.Case Title: C. L. VS. MOBILITY HOLDINGS, LIMITED ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion For Leave To File Cross-Complaint
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Friday, July 10, 2026, Line 7, DEFENDANT THE NEW WHEEL, INC.'s Motion For Leave To File Cross-Complaint. 1 - Defendant The New Wheel's motion for leave to file a cross-complaint is DENIED. Movant's citation CCP 426.50 and the bad faith standard of Silver Organizations Ltd. v. Frank (1990) 217 Cal.App.3d 94 is off point. The proposed cross-complaint for equitable indemnity, implied indemnity, negligence, contribution, and declaratory relief is a permissive cross-complaint subject to the requirements of CCP 428.10. "To be considered a compulsory cross-complaint, a related cause of action must have existed at the time of the service of [the] answer." (Crocker Nat. Bank v. Emerald (1990) 221 Cal.App.3d 852, 864.) The proposed indemnity claims have yet to accrue. (See Crouse v. Brobeck, Phleger & Harrison (1998) 67 Cal.App.4th 1509, 1541 ["a tort defendant's equitable indemnity action is separate and distinct from the plaintiff's tort action against the defendant and does not arise for statute of limitations purposes until the defendant pays a judgment or settlement for which he is entitled to indemnity"]; Greystone Homes, Inc. v. Midtec, Inc. (2008) 168 Cal.App.4th 1194, 1209 ["a defendant may pursue a comparative equitable indemnity claim against other tortfeasors either (1) by filing a cross-complaint in the original tort action or (2) by filing a separate indemnity action after paying more than its proportionate share of the damages through the satisfaction of a judgment or through a payment in settlement."].) In addition, "[t]here are no compulsory cross-complaints against parties other than plaintiff." (The Rutter Group California Practice Guide: Civil Procedure Before Trial 6:524 (2025).) Tjarko Leifer is presently not a party to this case. In the interests of justice, the motion is denied. Allowing the cross-complaint will lead to a trial delay. Lastly, movant is not prejudiced. It can argue comparative fault at trial. It can also bring an independent action for indemnity.
